priority_resolution.raw_vs_final: RAW_STATE_BOOLEAN and FINAL_PRIORITY_RESOLVED_STATE are distinct and both recovered; the raw booleans overlap, the final label does not
priority_resolution.corroborates_frozen: the frozen definition's priority exclusions (T4 46,160 / T1G 2,008 / T6 632 / T2G 313) are consequences of this order

hidden_dependencies.name: prev1IsBear includes a prior doji
hidden_dependencies.why_it_matters: a formula-only reading would use 'previous bar bearish'; the source counts a prior doji as bearish, which changes the eligible population for every T state built on it
hidden_dependencies.corroborates: the frozen T1 text says exactly this — 'prev1IsBear (close[1]<open[1] OR doji[1])'

hidden_dependencies.name: fullyEngulfs depends on two user INPUTS
hidden_dependencies.recovered: eHigh >= ePH and ePL >= eLow and bodyRatioOk
hidden_dependencies.why_it_matters: the source does not fix these values; the materialisation used whatever was set when the export ran, and that configuration is recorded nowhere
hidden_dependencies.resolved_by: the input sweep above, which identifies the body-based default

hidden_dependencies.name: Z7_clean is cross-family
hidden_dependencies.recovered: Z7_raw and not anyOtherBullRaw and not anyOtherBearRaw
hidden_dependencies.why_it_matters: the doji state only fires when NO other bull or bear raw state does, so it cannot be evaluated per-family in isolation

hidden_dependencies.name: the emitted label passes through display toggles
hidden_dependencies.detail: tBase applies showT1, showT4, ... to bullCode before producing a label
hidden_dependencies.why_it_matters: if the materialised column came from tBase rather than bullCode, a disabled toggle would suppress a state entirely; with the defaults the two coincide

legacy_conformance.method: the recovered semantics were executed against the legacy bars table and the resulting label compared to materialised t_sig, exactly, including the priority chain
legacy_conformance.target: legacy `bars` (daily, 2021-05-26 .. 2026-08-25), deduplicated one row per (ticker, date) with sp500 < nasdaq < russell2k

input_sweep.note: no configuration reaches exactness; useWick=True is decisively worse (92-93%), confirming the body-based default
input_sweep.why_searched: the source fixes the FORMULAS but not the INPUT VALUES used at materialisation time; recovering them is part of recovering the semantics, and this search is X-only

dominant_class.name: STORAGE_PRECISION_ROUNDING
dominant_class.evidence: 74.1% of residuals (33,600 of 45,358) sit on a bar whose current or prior body is at most $0.011
dominant_class.mechanism: `bars` stores OHLC rounded to two decimals; Pine computed on full precision. On low-priced names the rounding destroys the sign of sub-cent bodies, so isBull/isBear/isDoji flip.
dominant_class.worked_example: AACB 2025-04-11 stored open 9.88 close 9.88 is materialised T10, which requires close > open — impossible at the stored values, ordinary at full precision
dominant_class.concentration: nasdaq 34,764 and russell2k 10,078 versus sp500 516; the effect scales with how large a cent is relative to the price
dominant_class.relation_to_frozen_artifact: this IS the 'feed/tick class' the frozen T1 definition named. It is now explained rather than labelled.

unexplained.note: not absorbed into the rounding account; 26% of residuals remain uncharacterised and are recorded as such

residual_inventory.why_not_priority_defect: a priority defect can only REASSIGN among simultaneously firing states; it cannot make a state fire where every recovered predicate is false, which is the largest residual class

z_discovery.what: a complete thirteen-state bearCode priority chain mirroring bullCode
